mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when GDP growth is positive, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in unemployment suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when unemployment exceeds 10%, more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When employment increases but unemployment also rises, it may indicate inefficiencies, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when both series move in opposite directions, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate indicates tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when FEDFUNDS exceed 4%, more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation as indicated by CPI suggests decreased consumer spending, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when CPI exceeds 250, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production alongside GDP growth indicates supply chain issues, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when INDPRO declines while GDPC1 rises, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when housing starts increase, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Declining real sales with high federal funds indicate stagflation, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when RSAFS declines and FEDFUNDS are high, more than 50% of the time.
